data.narrative:
Avalanche Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Robin Langtry and Brian Riordan that has raised $80M to date. The target sits within a sector peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Lenz Energy, LNZA), including notable private peers such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Valuation analysis relied on a single applicable method due to data constraints. Stage-progression methodology, anchoring to the $80M total raised as a proxy for current value, applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A to subsequent-stage advancement, yielding an implied valuation of $160M. A peer-median approach was not applicable: while 9 same-sector peers exist, insufficient datapoints met narrow filtering criteria (same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar valuation tier), with only 3 required minimum unmet. Applying an all-sector median would risk substantial distortion.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $136M (low) to $184M (high), centered on $160M. This single-method triangulation carries meaningful uncertainty, particularly around stage-progression multiplier appropriateness for this company's specific risk profile and market conditions. The limited peer set underscores that comparable-company corroboration remains unavailable. Key sensitivities include execution risk, frontier-tech capital intensity, and sector funding environment volatility. Additional comparable data at similar stage and valuation tier would strengthen conviction.
